headline: High: AutoGen and n8n both have default shell/write/network capabilities, creating dangerous cross-agent action and data-flow risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and emit tool-driven outputs; n8n can ingest workflow inputs and server files. A shared filesystem or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented. The pathway is plausible in default deployments, not provably blocked.
conditions: IF AutoGen writes untrusted content into a directory n8n reads
IF n8n workflow steps parse AutoGen output as instructions or code
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files
Add a manual review step before n8n consumes AutoGen output
Use content tagging to distinguish data from instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance checks between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and has broad network egress; n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and can access server files plus many integrations. If sensitive application data enters AutoGen and is then passed into n8n workflows or external nodes, leakage can occur in default configurations. The pair’s shared file and API surfaces make this materially risky.
conditions: IF sensitive application data is passed from AutoGen into n8n workflows
IF any n8n integration node forwards that data to an external service
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate data classes
Turn off unnecessary n8n integration nodes
Store secrets outside shared workflow inputs
Review outbound destinations before execution
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read and write files, and use broad network egress. AutoGen’s isolation is configurable, while n8n’s Execute Command is explicitly not sandboxed. Without explicit locking or directory separation, concurrent writes and side effects can collide in the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path
IF either agent uses Execute Command or shell writes concurrently
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Disable n8n Execute Command where possible
Serialize jobs touching the same resources
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen produces agent outputs that n8n can consume as workflow inputs, and n8n can then trigger actions through its integration nodes. If n8n treats AutoGen output as authoritative without verification, a mistaken or malicious upstream result can cascade into external side effects. The pair therefore has a default path from generated content to action-taking.
conditions: IF n8n workflow steps use AutoGen output without validation
IF downstream nodes perform external actions based on that output
mitigations: Insert a human approval gate before actions
Validate AutoGen outputs against schemas
Limit n8n nodes to read-only operations
Log and diff proposed actions before execution
requires-engineering: add policy checks on workflow triggers

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen and n8n both expose server-side file and network surfaces, but the profiles do not specify concrete residency or certification mismatches. The main compliance concern is differing retention and logging behavior across workflow data and agent outputs, which can affect the same data class in practice. Because the exact policies are undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF workflow data includes regulated personal data
IF n8n retention or logging exceeds AutoGen handling policies
mitigations: Minimize regulated data in shared workflows
Review retention settings in both systems
Disable verbose logging for sensitive runs
Separate environments by data class
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
